title: Never played London; Stockholm and Montreux; finding the 'Sugar' album
summary: He never played London but did play Stockholm and Montreux; Wilson reads off the details of the Sugar album, recorded in the Black Forest on April 1-2, 1968.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Excellent. But anyhow, so the two trips you went to Europe, you never played in London, and you did --
No! Not one --
: -- get to Stockholm?
Oh yes. We left (unintelligible) 2nd we were going to Stockholm, and other thing, and I think I asked you, Switzerland there, and mentioned a friend of yours -- Simmen Johnny Simmons.
: Johnny Simmons.
Yeah (Laughs). Johnny.
: At Montreux, you played Montreux, didn't you, the first time around?
Oh, yes.
: But now the record that you made, Sugar, that was made in Germany?
Yes. Can I hold it for a minute?
Sure. Sure.
(Recording interruption.)

We found the record. It's 'Sugar,' by the Saints and Sinners in Europe. It's on the MPS label, and it was recorded in Villingen, in the Black Forest on April 1st and 2nd, 1968. And that was right after your first European tour. Right?
Yes.

At the end of this -- two days after you finished your European tour. And you played 'Sugar,' Blues in My Heart, Little Rock Getaway, If I Had You, 'The Hucklebuck,' You Know What it Means to Miss New Orleans --
That's the one I --
-- 'Soft Buns' -- that's one of Red's pieces? -- 'After Hours,' and 'Canadian Sunset.'
Uh-huh, and then the vocal on Do You Know What it Means --
You did the vocal on You Know What it Means.
Uh-huh. Yeah.
And there's a picture of you with your mute, too.
(Laughter.)
In the album.
You've got to hear this.
I'll hear it. I'll hear it.
We'll have to stick You've got to stop and let's take it
in there. You've got to hear it.
: I'll hear it. Don't worry.
Because I'm very proud of it. I'm very proud of the recording, and the thing I want you to just hear this, that -- that tune.
: Okay.
So I -- want me to when we find the other thing and play it.
